title: Drummers trading jobs: J. C. Heard, Cozy Cole, Raymond Scott and Sid Catlett
summary: Jones recounts how he steered J. C. Heard to Cab Calloway and Cozy Cole to Raymond Scott's CBS band, with Sid Catlett staying with Teddy Wilson.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: girl, you just wait." I told everybody, "You just wait; Cozy he can play." Then they'd say, "Is he all right?" I'd say, "Yeh, but Sidney, you're larger than me. If he come in here and be doing a thing wrong while I'm out of town, you bop him across his head." So we checked into the Norwood Hotel - you remember the Norwood?
Sure, in Detroit, Michigan, J. C.'s home town.
Right. So I got the key to 913 King Street. They know I'm going to stay there - I don't stay at the hotel, I just get a room there.
That's where he lived. 913 King Street still.

That's where I live. So we go there and he said, "Guess what?" I said, "You're going with Teddy Wilson. Don't you play drums till I come to New York." Sure enough, little J. C. came on in. Then in ensuing things, we were going through a period - I was with the name and what's that was writing Mr. John Hammond, I was with Raymond Scott... I went into down beat Rockefeller Center and we were trying to break through. Raymond Scott wanted somebody to get on his radio show and I said, "Sidney, you take the job -"
When did he play with Benny Goodman?

No, the big band, and Johnson was on bass, and Coottie was there, you see. So what happened was everybody made a change but me. J. C. switched from Teddy, from Cafe Society, to go to play with Cab. Meanwhile you were right there in California when we Big Log Chicken and I said, "Cozy, you going to have to go on the staff and play with Raymond Scott." Cab didn't want him to leave. I said, "You have to leave, Fess, because we have to make a move out of here. You can't get Sidney; you'll have to take J. C." So J. C. came out to take Cozy's place with Cab. Cozy went with Raymond Scott. Sidney stayed with Teddy Wilson. I couldn't go with Benny Goodman. I had to stay in there because -
